domains.name: Voice Gateways and Session Border Controllers

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the CCNP Collaboration 350-801 Core certification exam with 120 minutes of testing across six technical domains.
editorial.overview: The CCNP Collaboration 350-801 Core examination tests professional competence with a duration of 120 minutes. Candidates are evaluated across six distinct domains, including infrastructure and design, protocols and endpoints, on-premises call control weighted at thirty percent, voice gateways and session border controllers, cloud and hybrid services at twenty-five percent, and media and QoS.
editorial.who_should_take: Network engineers and collaboration professionals with experience implementing core collaboration technologies should take this certification exam to validate their skills and advance their technical careers.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review official exam topics provided by Cisco. Focus study sessions on the six core domains, paying close attention to weights like the thirty percent allocated to on-premises call control and twenty-five percent to cloud and hybrid services. Practice relevant technical configurations and review all material.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers infrastructure and design concepts related to collaboration networks, accounting for fifteen percent of the evaluation, which requires careful study of standard networking principles and architectural requirements.

This section focuses on protocols and endpoints used in Cisco collaboration environments, representing ten percent of the total scope, where candidates must understand standard signaling protocols and specific endpoint configurations.

This content area addresses on-premises call control systems, making up thirty percent of the exam content, and requires extensive knowledge of call routing mechanisms, dial plans, and centralized call control features.

This domain evaluates voice gateways and session border controllers, accounting for ten percent of the evaluation by testing integration techniques, border element configurations, and gateway troubleshooting procedures for enterprise networks.

This area examines cloud and hybrid services, representing twenty-five percent of the total content, focusing on cloud integration strategies, hybrid architecture deployments, and service management tools provided by Cisco.

This final domain covers media and QoS principles, comprising ten percent of the exam domains, with an emphasis on media stream handling, bandwidth management, and quality of service configurations across networks.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your time carefully during the 120 minutes allowed for the test. Read each question carefully and address each domain according to its specified weight to maximize your overall score.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: Cisco does not publicly publish the exact question count for this 120 minutes exam, so candidates should check directly with Cisco for any current details regarding the exact number of questions across the 6 domains.
The passing score is determined by Cisco and is not publicly disclosed in the official exam topics document, so candidates should check with Cisco for specific scoring requirements.
The exam has a strict duration of 120 minutes, giving candidates a set amount of time to complete all questions across the six core domains covered on the test.

This certification exam is officially certified by Cisco as part of the CCNP Collaboration program, validating professional-level knowledge and technical implementation skills for enterprise networks.

methodology.summary: This detailed editorial page was built using verified facts from official exam topics and documentation provided directly by Cisco for candidate preparation and study planning.
